purpose: Close RESTORE-DRILL-001 — prove production PostgreSQL geo-redundant point-in-time-restore is operational end-to-end (trigger → provision → reachable → data present → cleanup).

verification.tcpReachableNotes: Network listener active; firewall denies probe from operator workstation, confirming network-level access controls are intact on restored servers (expected secure default).

cleanup.verificationMethod: az postgres flexible-server show returned ResourceNotFound
cleanup.estimatedCostNotes: Standard_D2s_v3 GeneralPurpose at ~$0.14/hr * ~0.85hr provisioned + storage prorated.

controlsValidated: Production PG geo-redundant backups are recoverable to a fresh server.
Restore preserves PostgreSQL version 16, SKU, and 256 GB storage.
Restore includes the live production database `nzila_os_prod` (not just system DBs).
Restored server enforces firewall by default (no public ingress until rules added).
Restore window covers the full configured 30-day retention (earliest = 2026-05-11).
Cleanup path is non-destructive to source and verifiable.
outOfScopeNotes: Drill validated restore mechanics + data presence. Application-level integration validation (point Union Eyes prod app at restored DB, run smoke + invariant tests) is the next-level test and is captured separately as DR-RUNBOOK-002 (not pilot-blocking).
Drill did not exercise geo-pair regional failover to a different Azure region; current geo-redundant backup setting supports it but a regional-failover drill is tracked as DR-RUNBOOK-003.

reviewer.performedBy: support@onelabtech.com (operator) + Copilot CLI agent (execution + evidence capture)
reviewer.signOffNotes: Drill executed end-to-end with full evidence capture. Source production server unaffected. Cost contained via immediate cleanup.
